subject: Copywriting
title: Rosie the Riveter
description: Learn Rosie the Riveter in one minute.

hook.text: 'We Can Do It!' Rosie the Riveter was a propaganda poster designed to recruit women into wartime factories.

buildup.text: J. Howard Miller designed the poster for Westinghouse in 1943.

discovery.text: Six million women entered the workforce during WWII.

twist.text: After the war, new propaganda told women to return home. The same tools that liberated were used to re-confine.

climax.text: Rosie proves propaganda can reshape identity. 'We Can Do It!' didn't just sell a job—it redefined who women could be.

punchline.text: Two weeks on display. 80 years of cultural impact. Copy reshapes identity.

quiz.question: How long was the original Rosie the Riveter poster displayed?
